title: CI/CD Pipelines and Docker for Testing

questions.prompt: In the lecture, Docker is introduced as the tool that solves which universal problem?
options: The 'it works on my machine' problem
questions.explanation: Docker solves the 'it works on my machine' problem by ensuring consistency everywhere, while CI/CD pipelines are described as the engine for automating software delivery.

questions.prompt: A team's pipeline automatically packages every successfully tested build and delivers it to a staging environment, but a person must approve each release to production. Which practice is this?
questions.explanation: Continuous Delivery extends CI by delivering tested builds to staging and keeps a manual gate before production; Continuous Deployment removes that gate and deploys every passing change to production without human intervention.

questions.prompt: What is the stated goal of Continuous Integration (CI)?
options: Find and fix integration bugs early and quickly through frequent commits
Keep code deployable at all times, with a manual gate before production
Automatically deploy every passing change directly to production
Validate the full system in a production-like staging environment
Perform a basic health check right after each deployment
questions.explanation: In CI developers commit frequently and each commit triggers a build and tests, with the goal of finding integration bugs early; keeping code deployable behind a manual gate is the goal of Continuous Delivery.

questions.prompt: Which order matches the stages of a CI/CD pipeline?
questions.explanation: Code is committed to version control (Source), compiled or packaged (Build), validated by automated tests (Test), deployed to pre-production for final validation (Staging) and then released to users (Deploy).

questions.prompt: In the test pyramid used for pipeline testing, what is the approximate distribution of tests?
questions.explanation: Unit tests form the wide base (~70%, fast and cheap, run first), integration tests the middle (~20%) and E2E tests the small top (~10%, slow and expensive but highest confidence).

questions.prompt: A new release has just been deployed and the team wants a basic health check to confirm it is working. Which test type does the pipeline testing table assign to this Deploy stage?
questions.explanation: Smoke tests run at the Deploy stage as a basic health check after deployment; E2E tests belong to the Staging stage, where the full system is validated in a production-like environment.

questions.prompt: Which benefit of Docker for testing refers to running tests in a clean, pristine environment every time, eliminating interference?
questions.explanation: Isolation gives every test run a clean environment; Consistency means identical environments for development, testing and production, and Scalability means spinning up containers on demand for parallel tests.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly compares containers with virtual machines?
options: Containers share the host kernel, while each VM runs a full guest OS
Containers start in minutes, while VMs start in a few seconds
Containers are gigabytes in size, while VMs are only megabytes
Containers give hardware-level isolation, VMs process-level isolation
Containers carry hypervisor overhead, while VMs run at near-native speed
questions.explanation: Containers share the host kernel, start in seconds, are megabytes in size, run at near-native speed and isolate at process level; VMs run a full guest OS on a hypervisor, start in minutes, are gigabytes in size and isolate at hardware level.

questions.prompt: In Docker terminology, what is an image?
options: A read-only template containing the application and its environment
A runnable, isolated instance created from a read-only template
A text file with instructions for building the application package
A public registry for storing and sharing application packages
A tool for defining and running multi-container applications
questions.explanation: An image is a read-only template (the 'class definition' or blueprint); a container is a runnable, isolated instance of it, a Dockerfile is the recipe that builds it and Docker Hub is the registry that stores and shares it.

questions.prompt: A tester needs to start a web application, its database and a cache together as one multi-container setup. Which Docker concept is designed for this?
questions.explanation: Docker Compose is the tool for defining and running multi-container applications (the 'orchestra conductor' for your services); a Dockerfile only holds the instructions to build one image.

questions.prompt: After installing Docker, which command runs a built-in container whose successful run confirms that the installation is complete?
questions.explanation: The second verification step, docker run hello-world, runs the built-in "hello-world" container; docker --version only checks which Docker version is installed.

questions.prompt: Which Docker command lists all containers, both running and stopped?
questions.explanation: docker ps -a lists all containers whether running or stopped; plain docker ps lists only running containers, and docker images lists local images.

questions.prompt: In the Python test Dockerfile, why are requirements.txt copied and the dependencies installed before the rest of the application code is copied?
options: For better caching of the dependency installation step
Because WORKDIR can only be set after pip has finished
Because COPY . . would otherwise delete installed packages
To make the final image read-only before the tests start
So that pytest runs automatically while the image is built
questions.explanation: The Dockerfile comment says dependencies are copied and installed first for better caching; the rest of the code is copied afterwards with COPY . .

questions.prompt: What does the instruction CMD ["pytest", "-v", "--html=report.html"] do in the Python test Dockerfile?
options: Defines the command that runs when the container starts
Runs pytest once while the image is being built
Installs pytest and the other listed dependencies
Sets the working directory inside the container
Selects the lightweight base image to start from
questions.explanation: CMD defines the command to run when the container starts, so docker run my-python-tests executes pytest; RUN pip install installs the dependencies, WORKDIR sets the directory and FROM picks the base image.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Jenkins, GitLab CI and GitHub Actions is correct?
options: Jenkins is self-hosted and highly configurable, with a steeper learning curve
GitHub Actions is self-hosted and configured with a Groovy Jenkinsfile
GitLab CI supports Docker only through plugins and is the easiest to learn
Jenkins is built into GitHub and is best suited to open-source projects
GitHub Actions is best for complex enterprise needs and maximum control
questions.explanation: Jenkins is self-hosted, highly configurable, supports Docker via plugins and has the steeper learning curve, suiting complex enterprise needs; GitHub Actions is built into GitHub, is the easiest to learn and suits GitHub-hosted and open-source projects.

questions.prompt: A project is hosted on GitLab and will use GitLab CI. Which file defines its pipeline configuration?
questions.explanation: GitLab CI is configured with .gitlab-ci.yml; Jenkins uses a Groovy-based Jenkinsfile and GitHub Actions uses YAML files under .github/workflows/.

questions.prompt: In a GitHub Actions workflow file, which key specifies the virtual machine environment for a job (for example ubuntu-latest)?
questions.explanation: runs-on selects the virtual machine environment for the job; on defines the triggering event, services spins up other containers such as a database, and steps lists the sequence of tasks.

questions.prompt: A team reorders its pipeline so that the quickest checks, unit tests and linting, run before the slower test suites. Which best practice is this?
questions.explanation: Fail Fast means running the quickest tests (unit, linting) first; Parallelize means running multiple test suites simultaneously using matrix builds or test sharding.

questions.prompt: What outcome did Etsy achieve after adopting robust CI/CD pipelines, Infrastructure as Code and fully integrated automated testing?
options: It grew from a few deployments per year to 50+ deploys per day
It grew from a few deployments per month to 5+ deploys per day
It grew from one deployment per week to thousands of deploys per day
It cut deployments to one per quarter in order to reach zero downtime
It grew from a few deployments per day to 50+ deploys per hour
questions.explanation: Etsy went from a few deployments per year to 50+ deploys per day with near-zero downtime and faster bug detection; 'thousands of code changes daily' describes Netflix.
